reason: The cited evidence (E3, E4, E5) supports that increasing elemental complexity raises failure temperatures against interdiffusion and that high entropy of mixing stabilizes phases, but it does not provide direct measurements of diffusion activation barriers, sluggish diffusion mechanisms, or specific activation energy differences (50–60 kJ/mol) in nanoalloys. The key mechanistic premises about lattice distortions increasing diffusion barriers and quantified diffusion suppression are therefore largely unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: High configurational entropy lowers Gibbs free energy and stabilizes single-phase solid solutions at high temperatures
Lattice distortions in multi-principal element alloys increase diffusion activation barriers
Sluggish diffusion in high-entropy alloys suppresses atomic migration and phase segregation
Diffusion activation energies in high-entropy nanoalloys are measurably higher (e.g., 50–60 kJ/mol) than in lower entropy alloys
High-entropy nanoalloys maintain homogeneous single-phase structure under high-temperature annealing
